title: Testing Distributional Treatment Effects in Wasserstein Distance under Shared Outcome Measurement Error
banked_reason: Supervisor stop: capped discovery after six revisions; assumption applicability of the all-frequency envelope class remains unresolved. NO-PASS after explicit angle-action give-up; mathematical refutation not established.
gap_reasons: The all-frequency positive lower envelope is load-bearing and far stronger than standard ordinary-smooth tail comparability; its justification establishes nonemptiness via Laplace mixtures but not realistic applicability.

The globally fixed upper envelope likewise tailors the error class to the proposed inverse argument without an independent scientific or measurement-error justification beyond a nonempty example class.
proof_attempt_summary: Six proposal revisions addressed literature coverage and empirical positioning. The final reviewer retained two C-assumption-impractical flags for the fixed all-frequency Fourier envelopes; the supervisor ordered give-up at the discovery cap. No F-stage Lean proofs were produced, and mathematical refutation was not established.
tldr: A mathematical shared-error deconvolution benchmark asks for the sharp main-sample budget for testing a zero marginal causal distributional effect against latent \(W_1\) separation \(\delta\), for every direct-error calibration budget \(m\). The full declared class has four positive Lipschitz densities on \([0,1]\), unknown overlapping propensities, known uniform stratum weights and one shared symmetric additive error satisfying \([2(1+t^2)]^{-1}\le\phi_\eta(t)\le2/(1+t^2)\) at every real frequency and \(\mathbb E[E^2]\le4\). Bounded centered Laplace-scale mixtures constitute a concrete nonempty subclass. The main obligation has two possible resolutions: certify that an original-record construction independent of calibration attains the matched order, with an unchanged-calibration-likelihood converse, or prove that calibration affects the order and derive its exact regimes from displayed bounds and a same-class converse. Signal-dependent endpoint approximation, conditional Hilbert covariance and compact Laplace likelihood perturbations are the construction handles. The benchmark is conditional on the declared global envelope; Chen and coauthors motivate only the causal no-effect question and provide no validation of the error or strata model. Known-error Wasserstein estimation, direct adversarial-loss testing and noisy homogeneity inference retain separate anchored comparisons.
gap: Known-error Wasserstein deconvolution rates concern one-law estimation. Direct Wasserstein two-sample rates have no convolution channel. Existing noisy homogeneity inference and Gaussian inverse testing establish important antecedents, but the inspected statements do not supply a uniformly matched latent-Wasserstein frontier with fixed risks on this complete original-record class.
fill: The open result evaluates \(S(\delta,m)\) uniformly over the full declared class using signal-dependent endpoint approximation, conditional real-Hilbert covariance and a same-class original-iid converse. It must either certify calibration-free attainment of the matched order or establish calibration dependence and derive the precise regimes from upper and lower bounds. Shared nonvanishing convolution preserves the standardized zero contrast; the latent-separation power calculation and randomized-test converse must determine whether this population fact permits calibration-free optimality. Uniform-stratum augmentation and finite stratum averaging give a direct-error two-sample specialization, with lower witnesses certified inside the balanced homogeneous restriction. The optional empirical-inverse accuracy budget is a separate construction bound and supplies no premise or transition for the main frontier.
